This is more than an internal component relay: the documented shadowing sends the agent's email to the external attacker-controlled tool (agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s4-mcp-rug-pull.md:8-15, agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:226-229).",

It also supplies no proxy-isolation test, so the structural facts remain unknown rather than supporting N.",

Argument validation is also disabled in the baseline, so this is a wide rather than independently constrained extension surface (agent-sec-lab/agent/config.py:22-23, agent-sec-lab/agent/tools.py:235-238).",

AT:P reflects the required attacker-controlled MCP connection, which the default CLI does not attach, while UI:P reflects the user's ordinary email request rather than approval of a malicious operation (agent-sec-lab/agent/__main__.py:9-21, agent-sec-lab/agent/loop.py:28-38, agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s4-mcp-rug-pull.md:8-15). Email disclosure and hijacked dispatch support VC:L/VI:L, without established availability or subsequent-system losses; the attacker owns the receiving MCP server, not the user's email information (agent-sec-lab/docs/writeups/s4-mcp-rug-pull.md:8-15)."
